mainTopic: Checking a בכור's blemish around יום טוב, moving a dead animal on יום טוב, and dividing an animal on יום טוב without setting prices
overview: The גמרא finishes describing how רבא handled a בכור around יום טוב. He looked at the blemish before יום טוב began, and on יום טוב itself he only asked how it happened, to make sure the owner did not cause it. A ברייתא proves from the words 'any blemish' that even causing a blemish indirectly is forbidden. A new משנה then rules that an animal that died may not be moved on יום טוב, and the same ruling was given to רבי טרפון about טמא חלה. The גמרא asks whether this goes against רבי שמעון, who allows cutting up a carcass for dogs. After working through two reports of רבא's view, it concludes that the משנה is about a קדשים animal that was already in danger of dying, and it is forbidden because it is holy. A second new משנה teaches that people may not first sign up for shares of an animal on יום טוב. The גמרא explains that the problem is setting prices, and it shows how to divide the animal by comparison or by fractions and settle the money after יום טוב.

steps.title: On יום טוב רבא only asked how it happened
steps.stepSummary: רבא did not examine the blemish on יום טוב itself. He only asked how the blemish came about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on יום טוב he would only ask how the incident happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing רבא's practice. He already looked at the blemish before יום טוב, so on יום טוב itself he only asked questions about how it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The actual checking of the מום was done while it was still a weekday. On יום טוב, רבא only found out the cause, so that he could make sure nobody made the blemish on purpose. This keeps him from doing the full examination on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And on the Festival he would only ask
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, who already looked at the blemish before יום טוב began.

phrases.english: how the incident happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of רבא's procedure from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, רבא only asked how the blemish happened. He did not do the examination then.

steps.title: A firstborn brought to רבא on the eve of the Festival
steps.stepSummary: A man brought a בכור to רבא near nightfall on ערב יום טוב. רבא saw the blemish and told him to come back the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of a man who brought a בכור to רבא toward evening on ערב יום טוב. רבא was sitting and washing his head. He looked up and saw the blemish, and told him: Go now and come back tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רבא's practice in action. This is the first part, which happens before יום טוב starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא saw the מום while it was still ערב יום טוב, so the looking was done in time. He did not decide the case yet, though. He sent the man away until the next day, which was יום טוב, to finish up.

phrases.english: Like that case of a certain man
who brought a firstborn animal before Rava
toward evening on the eve of the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָא חָיֵיף רֵישֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: Rava was sitting and washing his head.
He raised his eyes and saw its blemish.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל הָאִידָּנָא וְתָא לִמְחַר.
phrases.english: He said to him: Go now, and come back tomorrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 1 through a real story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blemish was seen before יום טוב, and the decision was left for the next day.

steps.title: רבא asks how the blemish happened
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב, רבא asks the owner how the blemish came about.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came the next day, רבא said: How did the incident happen?
steps.whatsHappening: Now it is יום טוב, and רבא does exactly what step 1 said. He only asks how it happened. This sets up the owner's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has already seen the מום, so he does not need to examine it again. He only needs the story, to make sure the blemish came about on its own.

phrases.english: When he came the next day,
he said: How did the incident happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story on the next day, which is יום טוב.

steps.title: The owner explains the thorn fence
steps.stepSummary: Barley was on one side of a thorn fence. The animal pushed its head through to eat, and a thorn split its lip.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Barley was scattered on one side of a thorn fence, and the animal was on the other side. When it wanted to eat, it pushed its head through, and a thorn split its lip.
steps.whatsHappening: The owner answers רבא's question. He describes how the blemish happened by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From this story, the blemish looks like an accident. But the barley happened to be right where it tempted the animal into the thorns. That sets up רבא's next question.

phrases.english: He said to him: Barley was scattered
on this side of a thorn fence,
and it was on the other side.
When it wanted to eat,
it pushed its head through
and a thorn split its lip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal split its lip on a thorn while reaching through a fence for barley.

steps.title: Did you cause it on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the owner placed the barley there on purpose to cause the blemish. The owner says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps you caused it? He said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks whether the owner set up the accident. The owner denies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner had placed the barley there to make the animal hurt itself, he would have caused the מום. Causing a blemish is forbidden, and the next steps prove that. Once the owner says no, the blemish can be treated as a real accident.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the whole reason רבא asked how it happened. He had to rule out a blemish that was caused on purpose.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא אַתְּ גְּרַמְתְּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps you caused it?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the owner's story to rule out a blemish caused on purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the owner deliberately caused the blemish.

steps.title: Where do we learn that causing a blemish is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that indirectly causing a blemish is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that causing a blemish is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story and asks for a source. It wants to know why רבא was worried about the owner causing the blemish. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question in step 5 assumed that causing a מום, even indirectly, is not allowed. The גמרא now asks where that rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do you say

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that causing a blemish is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule that רבא's question assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that causing a blemish indirectly is forbidden.

steps.title: The extra word 'any' forbids causing a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'any blemish' that one may not even cause a blemish indirectly, such as by putting dough on the ear for a dog to bite.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'There shall be no blemish in it.' From this I only know that it must not have a blemish. From where do we know that one may not cause it a blemish through something else? For example, he should not bring dough or a dried fig and put it on its ear so that a dog will come and take it. The פסוק says 'any blemish.' It says 'blemish,' and it also says 'any blemish.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns the rule from an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'blemish' alone forbids making a מום directly. The added word 'any' (כל) widens the ban to include causing a blemish indirectly, like getting a dog to bite the ear. The owner in the story could have done something like that, which is why רבא asked him.

keyTerms.meaning: any; all (the extra word that teaches the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Making a blemish on a holy animal is forbidden. Because the פסוק says 'any blemish,' even causing one indirectly is forbidden. That is why רבא asked how the blemish happened.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'There shall be no blemish in it,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ מוּם,
phrases.english: I only know that it must not have a blemish;
from where do we know that one may not cause it one
through something else,
that he should not bring dough or a dried fig
and place it on its ear
so that a dog will come and take it —
phrases.notes: The dog would bite off the food and nip the ear, leaving the animal with a blemish.

phrases.english: the verse says: 'any blemish.'
It says 'blemish,' and it says 'any blemish.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'any' in 'any blemish' forbids causing a blemish indirectly.

steps.title: A dead animal may not be moved on the Festival
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if an animal died, one may not move it from its place on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal that died — one may not move it from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that an animal that died on יום טוב may not be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, the reason seems to be מוקצה: the animal was alive when יום טוב began, so nobody planned to use it. The גמרא later explains the case differently. Steps 13–16 conclude that the משנה is about a קדשים animal that was already in danger of dying, and it is forbidden because it is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: an item set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: MISHNAH: An animal that died —
one may not move it from its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that died on יום טוב may not be moved from its place.

steps.title: רבי טרפון asks the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון was asked about a dead animal and about חלה that became טמא. The study hall told him neither may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident: they asked רבי טרפון about a dead animal and about חלה that became טמא. He went into the בית המדרש and asked, and they told him: One may not move them from their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its ruling with a story. In it, the חכמים give the same ruling for both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story adds a second case, טמא חלה, which no one is allowed to eat. The חכמים rule that both the dead animal and the טמא חלה stay where they are on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: A dead animal and טמא חלה both may not be moved on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And there was an incident, and they asked Rabbi Tarfon
about it and about the challah that became impure,
phrases.notes: "It" means the dead animal from the start of the משנה.

phrases.english: and he went into the study hall and asked,
and they told him: One may not move them from their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 8 with a real incident and adds the case of טמא חלה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a dead animal may not be moved on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling the בית המדרש gave to רבי טרפון.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the unnamed משנה forbidding a dead animal disagrees with רבי שמעון, who lets one cut up a dead animal for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we say our unnamed משנה is not like רבי שמעון? In another משנה, רבי שמעון says you may cut up gourds for an animal and a dead animal for dogs. רבי יהודה says: if it was not already dead before שבת, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by suggesting that our משנה, which forbids moving a dead animal on יום טוב, clashes with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a carcass only if the animal died on שבת itself. So רבי שמעון, who argues with him, seems to permit even an animal that died on שבת. That looks like the opposite of our משנה, which forbids moving it.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed teaching; a משנה stated with no name attached
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; a carcass

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה of רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה is about שבת, not יום טוב. The גמרא assumes the same מוקצה rules apply to both here.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shall we say we learned an unnamed משנה
that is not like רבי שמעון?
(As we learned:) רבי שמעון says:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Either way, this is a quote from a משנה in שבת 156b.

phrases.english: We may cut up gourds for an animal,
and a carcass for the dogs.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: if it was not a carcass
from before שבת, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the גמרא's attention to the משנה from step 8 and asks whose view it follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה forbidding moving a dead animal on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון permits a carcass for dogs even when the animal died on שבת, so a ruling that forbids it seems to go against him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees about animals that died
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה can follow רבי שמעון, because he agrees that animals which died on the day itself are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי שמעון: he agrees that living animals that died are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can still match רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Living animals that died" means an animal that was healthy when the day began. Nobody planned to give it to the dogs, so even רבי שמעון treats it as מוקצה. The carcass רבי שמעון permits must be one that was expected to die.

phrases.english: You can even say it is רבי שמעון,
for רבי שמעון agrees
about living animals that died, that they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: רבי שמעון's leniency does not cover animals that died unexpectedly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון permits every carcass, so the משנה goes against him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון also forbids an animal that died unexpectedly, so the משנה fits his view.

steps.title: But one version of רבא says רבי שמעון permits it
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for מר בר אמימר's version of רבא, but מר בריה דרב יוסף quotes רבא saying that רבי שמעון permits even animals that died on the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for מר בר אמימר, who quotes רבא saying רבי שמעון agrees that animals that died are forbidden. But מר son of רב יוסף quotes רבא saying רבי שמעון disagreed even about animals that died and permits them. What can we say according to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the last answer only works for one of two reports of what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two students report רבא differently. If רבי שמעון permits even animals that died unexpectedly, the answer of step 11 falls apart, and our משנה seems against רבי שמעון again.

phrases.english: This works well for מר בר אמימר
in the name of רבא, who said:
רבי שמעון agreed
about living animals that died, that they are forbidden; that is fine.
But for מר, son of רב יוסף,
in the name of רבא, who said:
רבי שמעון disagreed
even about living animals that died, that they are permitted:
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון agrees animals that died are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the other report of רבא, רבי שמעון permits even these, so the contradiction with the משנה returns.

steps.title: זעירי: the משנה is about a holy animal
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that the משנה is talking about a קדשים animal that died.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי explained it as speaking about a קדשים animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works even for מר בריה דרב יוסף's report of רבא, where רבי שמעון permits animals that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead קדשים animal may not be used for any benefit, so it cannot be given to dogs. That is why it may not be moved, even according to the version of רבא in which רבי שמעון permits animals that died. On this reading, the משנה is not about an ordinary animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside as holy, for the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: The ban now comes from the animal being holy, not from מוקצה. As step 15 shows, this creates a new problem for the other version of רבא.

phrases.english: זעירי explained it:
as speaking about a holy animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about an ordinary animal, so it goes against רבי שמעון's lenient view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a holy animal, which is forbidden for a different reason. That lets the משנה fit רבי שמעון even in מר בריה דרב יוסף's lenient version of רבא.

steps.title: Proof: the animal is paired with חלה
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the משנה supports זעירי: the animal is listed together with חלה, which is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording shows this too. It says they asked "about it and about חלה that became טמא." Just as חלה is holy, the animal is also holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up זעירי's answer from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question put to רבי טרפון joins the dead animal with טמא חלה. Since חלה is holy, it makes sense that the animal in the same question is holy too.

keyTerms.meaning: The piece of dough given to a כהן; it is holy

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is about a dead קדשים animal, like the טמא חלה it is paired with. The next step shows this still leaves a problem for one version of רבא.

phrases.english: The wording shows this too, since it teaches:
"about it and about the חלה that became טמא."
Just as the חלה is holy,
so too the animal is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 13 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: זעירי's explanation that the animal is holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The pairing of the animal with טמא חלה in the question to רבי טרפון

steps.title: זעירי's answer only fits one version of רבא
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה forbids the dead animal only because it was קדשים, then a regular animal that died would be allowed. That fits מר בריה דרב יוסף's version of רבא, but not מר בר אמימר's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the only reason is that the animal was holy, which means a regular animal would be allowed. That works for מר בריה דרב יוסף quoting רבא, who said רבי שמעון disagreed even about animals that died and allowed them. But for מר בר אמימר quoting רבא, who said רבי שמעון agrees that animals that died are forbidden, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on זעירי's answer from Step 13. It shows that this answer only works with one of the two versions of רבא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי said the problem was that the animal was קדשים. That means a regular (חולין) animal that died on יום טוב would be allowed. Only מר בריה דרב יוסף's version of רבי שמעון allows that. According to מר בר אמימר's version, רבי שמעון forbids even a regular animal that died on the day, so the משנה would fit neither רבי שמעון nor רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy, meaning an animal set aside for the בית המקדש
What is there to say? (the view has a problem)

phrases.english: Rather, the reason is that it was holy
but a non-holy one would be permitted.
This works out for מר son of רב יוסף
in the name of רבא, who said:
רבי שמעון disagreed

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים שֶׁמֵּתוּ שֶׁמּוּתָּרִין — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: even about animals that died, saying they are permitted. That is fine.
phrases.notes: Animals that died here means animals that died on יום טוב itself, like in Steps 11 and 12.

phrases.english: But according to מר bar אמימר
in the name of רבא, who said:
רבי שמעון agreed
about animals that died, that they are forbidden
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the זעירי answer that Step 14 had just supported
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's answer that the משנה is about a dead קדשים animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer implies that a regular animal that died on יום טוב is allowed. Only one version of רבי שמעון holds that, so under מר בר אמימר's version the משנה fits nobody.

steps.title: The animal was already in danger before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about an animal that was already sick and in danger before יום טוב, and in that case everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? An animal that was in danger of dying. In that case, everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The animal was already close to dying before יום טוב started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animal was already in danger before יום טוב, the owner expected it to die, so it was not totally unexpected. Even in מר בר אמימר's version, רבי שמעון would allow a regular animal like this. The animal in the משנה is forbidden only because it was קדשים, and קדשים may not be fed to dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow the case)
An animal in danger of dying

steps.whatToRemember: The dead-animal case in the משנה is a קדשים animal that was already in danger before יום טוב. A regular animal like that would be allowed according to רבי שמעון in both versions of רבא.

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
An animal in danger of dying, and this is everyone's view.
phrases.notes: The animal was already sick before יום טוב, so its owner expected it might die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about an ordinary animal that died suddenly, which מר בר אמימר's רבי שמעון forbids
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal was in danger before יום טוב, so all versions of רבי שמעון would allow a regular one. The משנה forbids it only because it was קדשים.

steps.title: New משנה: signing up for shares of an animal
steps.stepSummary: People may not sign up for shares of an animal on יום טוב itself. They may sign up on ערב יום טוב, and then slaughter and divide it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not sign up for a share of an animal for the first time on יום טוב. But one may sign up for it on ערב יום טוב, and then they slaughter it and divide it among themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how a group may share one animal on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arranging shares on יום טוב itself looks like doing business, which is a weekday activity. If the group arranged the shares before יום טוב, they may slaughter and divide the animal on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, for the first time

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not sign up for a share of an animal
for the first time on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִמְנִין עָלֶיהָ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: But one may sign up for it on ערב יום טוב,
and they slaughter it and divide it among themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נִמְנִין עַל הַבְּהֵמָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shares in an animal may not be first arranged on יום טוב. If they were arranged on ערב יום טוב, the group may slaughter and divide the animal on יום טוב.

steps.title: What does 'signing up' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly is forbidden in the משנה's phrase 'one may not sign up'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one may not sign up' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the משנה's words. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking part in a shared animal on יום טוב is clearly allowed, since the משנה lets them divide it. So the גמרא wants to know which part of 'signing up' is the problem.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What does 'one may not sign up' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה in Step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact action the משנה forbids with the phrase 'אין נמנין'

steps.title: Do not set prices on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that the forbidden part is setting a price for the shares of the animal on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One may not set a price for an animal for the first time on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. 'Signing up' means fixing how much money each share costs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming prices is what makes it look like business. Sharing the meat is allowed. Settling a money amount on יום טוב is the problem.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
One may not set a price for the first time
on an animal on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden 'signing up' is fixing a price for the animal on יום טוב

steps.title: So how should one do it?
steps.stepSummary: If prices may not be set, the גמרא asks how people can divide an animal on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should one do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question. It sets up רב's method in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People still need a way to know later how much each one owes. The גמרא wants a method that works without naming a price on יום טוב.

phrases.english: How should one do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on שמואל's rule from Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical way to share an animal on יום טוב without setting a price

steps.title: Compare two animals without naming a price
steps.stepSummary: רב says to put two animals side by side and ask whether one is like the other. After יום טוב they can work out the price from the other animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He brings two animals, stands them next to each other, and says: Is this one like that one?
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a way to divide the animal on יום טוב without talking about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody says a price. They only agree that the two animals are equal. After יום טוב, they can price the animal that was not slaughtered and figure out what each person owes.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is like that one

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may share an animal, but you may not name prices. Comparing it to another animal lets everyone work out the price after יום טוב.

phrases.english: רב said: He brings two animals
and stands them one next to the other,
and says: Is this one like that one?
phrases.notes: No price is mentioned. They only check that the two animals are equal, so the price can be worked out after יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare the slaughtered animal to a similar one, and set the actual price after יום טוב

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ban on naming a price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב one may not join a partnership in an animal for a set amount of money, like a סלע or two. One may join for a fraction, like half, a third or a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא: A person should not say to his friend on יום טוב, 'I am in with you for a סלע,' or 'I am in with you for two סלעים.' But he may say to him, 'I am in with you for half,' or 'for a third,' or 'for a quarter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the forbidden part is setting a price on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a money amount, like a סלע, is setting a price, so it is forbidden on יום טוב. Naming a fraction of the animal only divides the meat and says nothing about money, so it is allowed. This matches שמואל exactly, and it also fits רב's idea that the price is worked out after יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way: a ברייתא that supports what was just said
I am hereby with you, meaning I am your partner in this animal
A coin of a set value

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may divide an animal by fractions (half, third, quarter) but not by money (a סלע, two סלעים). The money is settled after יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: The partnership itself is not the problem. Only naming a money amount is forbidden. Joining for a share of the animal is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice how people can share meat on יום טוב without doing business-style pricing.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
A person may not say to his friend
'I am in with you for a סלע,'
'I am in with you for two,'
but he may say to him:
'I am in with you for half'
or for a third or for a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's explanation (step 19) and fits with רב's method of settling the price after יום טוב (step 21).
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's explanation that the forbidden 'signing up' in the משנה means setting a price for shares on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids joining for a money amount (a סלע or two) but allows joining for a fraction (half, third, quarter).
